'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Insurgency in the Maghreb (2002–present)|Insurgency in the Maghreb]]
**The death toll from yesterday's [[mass shooting]] at a [[Military base|military post]] near a [[Gold mining|gold mine]] in Inata, [[Soum Province]], [[Burkina Faso]], increases to 32, including 28 [[Gendarmerie|gendarmes]] and four civilians, making the attack the deadliest against security forces in the country. [https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/death-toll-northern-burkina-faso-attack-rises-32-2021-11-15/ (Reuters)]
*[[Liverpool Women's Hospital bombing]]
**Yesterday's taxi explosion in [[Liverpool]], [[England]], that killed the bomber and injured the driver outside the [[Liverpool Women's Hospital]], is declared a [[Terrorism in the United Kingdom|terrorist]] incident by [[Merseyside Police|police]]. [[Mayor of Liverpool|Mayor]] [[Joanne Anderson]] says that the driver locked the bomber inside the vehicle after noticing that the bomber was [[Suicide bombing|wearing an explosive device]]. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-england-merseyside-59291095 (BBC News)] [https://www.walesonline.co.uk/news/uk-news/liverpool-explosion-taxi-driver-hero-22166525 (WalesOnline)]
*Three [[Al-Shabaab (militant group)|al-Shabaab]] members escape from a maximum security prison in [[Kenya]], including one of the perpetrators of the [[Garissa University College attack|2015 Garissa attack]], in which 148 people were killed. [https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/three-terrorism-suspects-kenya-escape-prison-police-2021-11-15/ (Reuters)]

'''Business and economy'''
*[[Infrastructure policy of the Joe Biden administration]]
**[[President of the United States|U.S. President]] [[Joe Biden]] signs the [[United States dollar|$]]1.2 trillion [[Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act]] into law. [https://www.washingtonpost.com/politics/biden-poised-to-sign-12-trillion-infrastructure-bill-fulfilling-campaign-promise-and-notching-achievement-that-eluded-trump/2021/11/15/1b69f9a6-4638-11ec-b8d9-232f4afe4d9b_story.html (''The Washington Post'')]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[November 2021 Pacific Northwest floods]]
**[[Merritt, British Columbia]], [[Canada]] is evacuated after severe flooding inundated the city of about 7,000. Several highways throughout southern [[British Columbia]] were also washed out by heavy rain, leaving at least 10 people stranded. [https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/british-columbia/flooding-mudslide-evacuations-abbotsford-bc-1.6248963 (CBC)]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Cambodia]], [[Travel restrictions related to the COVID-19 pandemic]]
****[[Cambodia]] begins to allow [[COVID-19 vaccine|fully vaccinated]] foreign travellers to visit the country without a [[quarantine]] if they show a negative test result from the previous 72 hours and test negative again upon arrival, as the country currently has the one of world's highest COVID-19 vaccination rates. [https://www.barrons.com/articles/cambodia-re-opens-to-fully-vaccinated-travellers-01636953007 (AFP via ''Barron's'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in India]], [[Travel restrictions related to the COVID-19 pandemic]]
****[[India]] reopens its border to fully vaccinated foreign travellers on regular [[commercial flight]]s after being closed for 18 months since March 2020 due to a decrease in the number of new COVID-19 cases. All travellers must follow COVID-19 protocols and show a negative [[COVID-19 testing|test]] result from the previous 72 hours, except those from countries with mutual [[vaccine]] recognition. [https://apnews.com/article/coronavirus-pandemic-lifestyle-business-health-travel-4885c0d6ccaec33cd2606b0128a3f3b2 (AP)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Sri Lanka]], [[COVID-19 drug development]]
****[[Sri Lanka]] approves the use of the COVID-19 oral drug [[molnupiravir]] in the country. [http://www.adaderana.lk/news/78440/sri-lanka-approves-anti-covid-pill-molnupiravir (Adaderana)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Europe]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Germany]]
****[[Berlin]] begins to implement "2G" rule that limiting access to restaurants, cinemas, bars, and cultural and entertainment venues to those who are [[COVID-19 vaccination in Germany|vaccinated]] or have recovered from COVID-19 amid a rising number of COVID-19 cases across [[Germany]]. [https://www.voanews.com/a/germany-implements-new-covid-19-restrictions-as-cases-surge-/6314386.html (VOA)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Latvia]]
****[[Latvia]] ends its 8 p.m. to 6 a.m. curfew and allows companies to fire employees who are [[COVID-19 vaccination in Latvia|unvaccinated]] against COVID-19. Unvaccinated people are also banned from taking their duties for parliament and entering shopping malls with a size greater than {{convert|1500|m2}}. [https://medicalxpress.com/news/2021-11-latvia-toughens-unvaccinated-people.html (Medical Xpress)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom]], [[COVID-19 vaccination in the United Kingdom]]
****The [[Joint Committee on Vaccination and Immunisation]] approves the extension of age eligibility of COVID-19 vaccine [[booster dose]]s in the [[United Kingdom]] to people between 40 and 49 years old and the second dose for teenagers between the ages of 16 and 17 years. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2021/nov/15/uk-vaccine-advisers-set-to-approve-covid-booster-jabs-for-under-50s (''The Guardian'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Australia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Queensland]]
****[[Queensland]] reopens its state border to [[COVID-19 vaccination in Australia|fully vaccinated]] [[Australians]] travelling by plane, as 70% of the state's adult population are now fully vaccinated. [https://www.abc.net.au/news/2021-11-15/qld-coronavirus-covid-vaccine-border-reopen-cases/100620458 (ABC News Australia)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Egypt]]
***[[Egypt]] begins to ban [[COVID-19 vaccination in Egypt|unvaccinated]] public sector employees and university students from entering workplaces and universities unless they show a negative [[Polymerase chain reaction|PCR]] test from the previous 72 hours. [https://www.arabnews.com/node/1968551 (''Arab News'')]

'''International relations'''
*[[China–United States relations]]
**[[President of the United States|US President]] [[Joe Biden]] holds a virtual bilateral meeting with [[Paramount leader|China's leader]] [[Xi Jinping]]. [https://apnews.com/article/biden-xi-meeting-e6013378e03727b85a8f59f71fe61f4a (AP News)]
*[[Foreign relations of Kiribati]]
**The government of [[New Zealand]] vows to help islanders in [[Banaba]], [[Kiribati]], to access fresh water, as the island suffers from frequent droughts and is dependent on rainfall. [https://www.rnz.co.nz/international/pacific-news/455709/new-zealand-vows-to-help-to-get-water-to-kiribati-islanders (RNZ)]
*[[2021 Belarus–European Union border crisis]]
**The [[European Union]] says it will impose new sanctions on [[Belarus]] in response to the [[migrant crisis]] on the [[Belarus–Poland border]]. [https://edition.cnn.com/2021/11/15/europe/poland-belarus-border-crisis-nato-intl/index.html (CNN)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[2021 Argentine legislative election]]
**With nearly all votes counted, the ruling Peronist government loses control of both the [[Chamber of Deputies of Argentina|Chamber of Deputies]] and the [[Senate of Argentina|Senate]]. This is the first time since the return to democracy in 1983 that Peronists do not have a majority in either house. [https://www.elmostrador.cl/dia/2021/11/15/elecciones-legislativas-en-argentina-gobierno-de-alberto-fernandez-pierde-control-del-congreso-y-ofrece-dialogo-a-oposicion/ (''El Mostrador Chile'')]

'''Science and technology'''
*[[Russia]] carries out a direct-ascent [[anti-satellite weapon]] test on the defunct [[Soviet space program|Soviet spacecraft]] [[Kosmos 1408]], creating a cloud of debris that threatens the [[International Space Station]]. [https://spacenews.com/russia-destroys-satellite-in-asat-test/ (SpaceNews)]
